subject: Google Maps JavaScript KML Layer

evidence.claim: KmlLayer was deprecated as of April 30 2026.
Google recommends uploading KML as a dataset or using third-party libraries as alternatives.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: Migration pressure is real and alternatives exist, but the replacement space is already populated and consumer volume is not measured.

subject: Google Maps JavaScript DirectionsService
description: Google deprecated DirectionsService on February 25 2026; it is not yet scheduled for discontinuation and will continue to receive major-regression fixes with at least 12 months notice before support ends.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The installed base may be large, but immediate migration pressure is limited because Google has not scheduled discontinuation.

subject: Google Maps Platform client ID authentication

evidence.claim: Client IDs were deprecated May 26 2025 and could no longer be used after May 31 2026.
Google provides migration steps covering usage discovery, API keys, quota, code changes, monitoring, and deactivation.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: The sunset has already happened and Google documents a multi-step migration, making migration diagnostics or compatibility automation plausible; buyer demand remains unmeasured.

subject: GitHub REST rate endpoint rate property

subject: Google Merchant API v1beta

subject: MCP registry remote endpoint mismatch
description: A seeded sample of 1,200 MCP remote endpoints found 11.2% answered HTTP but did not perform the MCP initialize handshake at the advertised URL; the study cautions that these may be moved endpoints, retired paths, or pre-launch listings.

evidence.claim: In a sample of 1,200 of 10,542 unique remote endpoint URLs, 134 returned HTTP but did not speak MCP at the advertised path.
The author explicitly states the sample is not a census and that not-MCP does not prove the software is dead elsewhere.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: The registry contains a measurable integrity gap that can support endpoint-health or registry-quality tooling without taking control of third-party infrastructure.

subject: MCP registry deleted-server URL reservation
description: An MCP registry issue reports that deleting a server did not release its remote URL, blocking republishing under a verified domain namespace.

evidence.claim: A deleted registry entry continued to reserve its remote URL and produced a 400 error for a new publication using the same URL.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The residue is a concrete registry-state problem, but the fix may belong inside the registry rather than as a standalone external product.

subject: MCP namespace orphan after GitHub rename: skanfirmy

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: A clear orphaned-identity pattern exists, but the valid solution is namespace governance rather than acquisition.

subject: MCP namespaces orphaned after GitHub account rename

subject: MCP namespaces orphaned after organization rename

evidence.claim: The organization reported five stale namespace entries under atomno-labs after renaming to atomno-mcp and requested cleanup.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Multiple stale entries from one rename event show that namespace residue can occur at organizational scale rather than as isolated user error.

subject: MCP registry GitHub repository reachability residue
description: A community measurement of the MCP registry reported that 15.3% of 14,249 referenced GitHub repositories returned 404 at scan time, attributed to deletion, rename, or private state.

evidence.claim: The study scanned 14,249 unique GitHub repositories referenced by the registry and found 15.3% returning 404.
The study frames the result as a measured ecosystem effect rather than proof of malicious or dead software intent.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: The scale of stale repository references suggests a measurable registry-health intelligence problem; exact remediation demand still needs validation.

subject: MCP registry remote-domain concentration and stale paths
description: A registry audit found one domain associated with 75 separate namespaces, of which 62 returned text/html instead of completing an MCP handshake at the advertised path.

evidence.claim: An audit found one domain holding 75 registry entries across separate namespaces, with 62 serving text/html at the advertised MCP path.
The audit explicitly notes that this does not prove the products are fraudulent or that the software does not exist elsewhere.

decision.label: PURSUE
decision.reason: Concentration plus endpoint mismatch is a strong signal for registry-quality and observability tooling; the economic buyer remains to be validated.

subject: MCP registry publication propagation delay
description: Multiple registry issues document successful publication followed by persistent 404s or missing search visibility, sometimes lasting many hours or days.

evidence.claim: An official publication returned success but the direct endpoint remained 404 for more than 20 hours.
A separate case reported a successful publication still missing after more than two days.

decision.label: WATCH
decision.reason: The pain is concrete but may be fixed by registry infrastructure itself; external opportunity is primarily observability and support tooling.
